concepts.name: Punish forcing moves that leave the mover en prise
concepts.trigger: A capture or check is considered, but the moved piece will be immediately capturable by a lower- or equal-cost recapture with no compensation.
concepts.value_adjustment: Decrease move value strongly; add extra penalty if the moved piece is a major piece.
concepts.why: Repeated forcing moves won a tempo but then lost the moved piece on the next move, causing immediate material swings.

concepts.name: Do not sac queen/rook for check without forced gain
concepts.trigger: A checking move by queen or rook can be captured by the king or a simple defender and there is no forced tactical return.
concepts.value_adjustment: Apply very large penalty; only allow if immediate forced mate or clear net material gain is detected.
concepts.why: Checking major pieces were repeatedly captured at once, producing the largest losses in the dataset.

concepts.name: Pre-move recapture safety gate
concepts.trigger: Before finalizing any forcing move, opponent has an immediate legal recapture of the moved piece in one ply.
concepts.value_adjustment: Subtract value proportional to expected net material after the likely recapture sequence (at least one-ply horizon).
concepts.why: Many losses came from one-move blunders where an apparent active move failed basic recapture safety.

concepts.name: Respect legal king captures in tactical resolution
concepts.trigger: After giving check or trading near kings, a legal king capture of the attacking piece exists.
concepts.value_adjustment: Strongly downweight lines that ignore king captures; upweight lines that avoid placing capturable attackers next to the king.
concepts.why: Missing king-capture awareness caused direct tactical failures and lost major pieces.

concepts.name: Convert advantage by reducing volatility
concepts.trigger: Already ahead materially (large positive edge) but considering sharp forcing trades or speculative checks.
concepts.value_adjustment: Increase value of simplification and safety; penalize high-volatility tactics that risk hanging pieces or perpetual complications.
concepts.why: Large advantages were not converted, indicating poor risk control when winning.

concepts.name: Promotion-race urgency and blocker priority
concepts.trigger: Either side has a pawn one step from promotion or an imminent promotion race.
concepts.value_adjustment: Heavily reward moves that stop, check, or outrun promotion; penalize non-urgent moves that allow immediate promotion.
concepts.why: Endgame outcomes showed failure to convert and major value swings around imminent promotion events.

concepts.name: Low-clock pragmatism
concepts.trigger: Time remaining is low or game trend shows time-pressure collapse.
concepts.value_adjustment: Prefer fast, safe, low-branching moves; reduce value of complex speculative tactics requiring deep calculation.
concepts.why: A game was lost on time despite prior advantage, suggesting search/time policy should shift under clock stress.
